articleTitle: Stabilized Dispersion-Robust Millimeter-Wave Anything-Over-Fiber Transmitter in Access Networks Featuring a Double Sideband Suppressed Carrier Modulation
publicationTitle: 2023 International Workshop on Fiber Optics on Access Networks (FOAN)
abstract: In this paper we address the instability of a dispersion-resistant anything-over-fiber (AoF) transmitter with frequency doubling. This technology supports the evolution of higher-radio-frequency (RF) telecommunication systems operating in the millimeter-wave (mmW) range. The use of mmW communications has also gained attention in the area of optical access networks due to the increasing demand for higher data-transmission rates and the apparent spectrum congestion. However, the transmission of mmW signals over fiber-optic networks presents challenges related to the signal degradation caused by chromatic dispersion. In this paper a power-penalty-free transmission in the mmW range is enabled by an optical double-sideband transmitter with a suppressed carrier (ODSB-SC) based on a Mach-Zehnder-modulator (MZM). Due to its susceptibility to volatile operating conditions, the intended <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$U_{\pi}$</tex> bias voltage varies over time. Therefore, we propose a purely analog, closed-loop-control (CLC) system that continuously adjusts the bias voltage to provide the maximum suppression of the optical carrier at the MZM's output. We demonstrate experimentally the feasibility and performance of our proposed, stabilized, dispersion-robust mmW AoF transmitter. The results highlight the system's ability to achieve stable, dispersion-free mmW transmission over extended fiber links, making it a promising solution for next-generation access networks.

articleTitle: Effect of Macrobends on the Transmission Parameters of a High-Speed Coherent System
publicationTitle: 2023 International Workshop on Fiber Optics on Access Networks (FOAN)
abstract: The escalating demand for high-speed data transmission has led to the widespread deployment of coherent systems. In this study, we investigate the profound impact of macrobends on a cutting-edge 200 Gbit/s ADVA transmission system, employing an innovative robotic arm for precise assessments. Environmental factors can introduce attenuation into optical paths, curbing the achievable link range. Furthermore, the intricate modulation formats utilized in these systems render them susceptible to disruptions in the optical path. This paper delves into the critical importance of comprehending the effects of macrobends, as it enables the detection and prevention of theft of service (ToS) attacks. By harnessing a specialized measurement workstation equipped with a robotic arm, we gain valuable insights into the behavior of macrobends on the coherent transmission system. Additionally, we explore the promising approach of utilizing correlations between individual transmission parameter values to detect such events without the need for supplementary systems. Our findings demonstrate that malicious attempts involving macrobends introduce attenuation into the optical path, leading to observable changes in signal-to-noise ratio and bit error rate. Leveraging these parameter alterations, we establish a diagnostic method for identifying the execution of specific attacks. This research constitutes a significant step forward in enhancing the security and robustness of high-speed coherent optical networks.

articleTitle: Use of Fiber Optic Link for Phase-Noise Measurement
publicationTitle: 2023 International Workshop on Fiber Optics on Access Networks (FOAN)
abstract: The measurement of phase noise plays a critical role in the characterization of modern radio and optical systems. This paper explores the use of fiber optic links to quantify phase noise. It introduces the delay-line method for measuring phase noise and explains its advantages and limitations. It presents the photonic-delay phase-noise measurement method and its implementation using standard components in fiber-optic access network equipment. The importance of achieving quadrature locking in the mixer for accurate phase noise measurement is highlighted, along with the calibration process. The paper concludes with an example of phase noise characteristics in an opto-electronic oscillator.

articleTitle: ONU Interconnection for Reducing Latency in TWDM-PON Based Mobile Front- and Middle-Hauls by using Wavelength Mobility
publicationTitle: 2023 International Workshop on Fiber Optics on Access Networks (FOAN)
abstract: Due to the demands of ultra-large bandwidth and much reduced latency for current 5G and future 6G mobile networks, the fixed network infrastructure for mobile services is evolving rapidly to meet the needs of mobile operators [1]. The passive optical network (PON) is emerging as a very promising solution for 5G/6G mobile transport networks to provide the best total cost ownership (TCO) for its all-passive photonics (APP) nature. The time wavelength division multiplexing (TWDM-PON) can provide a larger capacity and more flexible bandwidth management than the legacy TDM-PON [2]. Here, a time/wavelength-division-multiplexing passive optical network (TWDM-PON) with virtual interconnection among optical network units (ONUs) is proposed to realize all-photonic networks providing large capacity, flexible bandwidth provisioning, and much reduced latency among the network nodes. The virtual interconnect among ONUs (vONUI) is achieved by simply adding a reflective channel filter at the remote node of the TWDM-PON and maintains its APP nature, as shown in Fig. 1. With this approach, the interconnect can be applied to all ONUs, not limited to adjacent nodes. The vONUI-enabled network can be used to serve as the middle-haul to connect the centralized unit (CU) and distributed units (DUs) as well as the front-haul to connect a DU with many radio units (RUs) for the 5G and beyond 5G mobile networks. The role of DUs in the functional split of 5G and beyond 5G era is to support low-latency for time-sensitive services. The RU interconnect (RUI) can help to achieve this goal by enabling direct communications among RUs, forwarding of timely data to neighboring RUs, and providing real-time up-stream bandwidth management. If the TWDM-PON is applied to serve as the middle-haul to connect CU and DUs, it forms an all-photonic switching networks among ONUs to provide direct interconnect among DUs (DUI) if each ONU is equipped with an extra wavelength for providing DUI. The DUI can improve mobile network performance by reducing latency, increasing flexibility, and enhancing reliability and security.

articleTitle: Passive Center-to-Clustered Edge Nodes Networks Using Thin-Film-Filter Based Wavelength Routers
publicationTitle: 2023 International Workshop on Fiber Optics on Access Networks (FOAN)
abstract: In a photonic network, wavelength routing is a key function. This article proposes thin-film-filter based wavelength router structure and its network application. The proposed network and wavelength router are basically passive, so they have attractive features of colorless, smaller latency and higher reliability. With path loss estimation, optical network simulations, and scalability discussions, possible area was clarified. They show the feasibility of the proposed structure.

articleTitle: Eavesdropping Vulnerabilities in Optical Fiber Networks: Investigating Macro-Bending-Based Attacks Using Clip-on Couplers
publicationTitle: 2023 International Workshop on Fiber Optics on Access Networks (FOAN)
abstract: Fiber optic cables have long been considered a secure medium that prevents eavesdropping due to their complexity. However, there are attack methods that allow eavesdropping or denial of service. These include methods based on bending optical fibers. The danger resides in the possibility of being able to carry out an attack without having to interrupt the path. To facilitate such attacks, it is possible to use a clip-on coupler. This coupler is designed to allow eavesdropping on the link without interruption. In this study, we focus on evaluating the coupling efficiency of a simple but commercially available clip-on coupler. This work investigates the effectiveness of jamming into the optical link, i.e., replicating the jamming attack and measuring it by simulating real traffic conditions. To better understand the complexity of these attacks, we perform additional measurements to investigate the effect of clip-on coupling on changes in the polarization state. Through this research, we highlight the increasing vulnerability of optical fibers to eavesdropping attempts, especially those using macro-based methods. By evaluating the performance of commercially available clip-on coupling, we provide valuable insights into potential risks and mitigation strategies for securing modern optical communication networks.

articleTitle: Demonstration of a Real-Time 100G Ethernet Space Division Multiplexing PON Using a Weakly Coupled Multicore Fiber
publicationTitle: 2023 International Workshop on Fiber Optics on Access Networks (FOAN)
abstract: We demonstrate a real-time 100G Ethernet transmission over space division multiplexing - passive optical network using a weakly coupled seven-core fiber in a point-to-multipoint layout. The application of this demonstration is targeting optical access networks, e.g., 5G/6G fronthaul. We perform RFC 2544 benchmarking and error-free 100G transmission to 25G optical network units using commercial transceivers and no additional digital signal processing.

articleTitle: A Self-Contained IoT Sensor Module for Realizing Drastic Cost Reduction
publicationTitle: 2023 International Workshop on Fiber Optics on Access Networks (FOAN)
abstract: This paper proposed a self-contained IoT sensor module which includes sensor for collecting various information, micro-computer and multiple solar panels for realizing dynamic cost reduction such as CAPEX and OPEX. Proposed module has the feature of automatically grasping the installation state such as the inclination and direction of the module using the time change of energy generated by solar panels and numerical analysis on the cloud. Furthermore, it is possible to supply power to drive the sensors using generated solar energy.

articleTitle: Spatial Hole Burning in Reflective Semiconductor Optical Amplifier: Numerical Analysis from the Standpoint of Classical Electromagnetism
publicationTitle: 2023 International Workshop on Fiber Optics on Access Networks (FOAN)
abstract: Electromagnetic modelling of reflective semiconductor optical amplifier (RSOA) is performed from the standpoint of classical electrodynamics, where loss or gain in a medium is described by means of complex permittivity. The steady-state frequency-domain analysis is carried out by the method of single expression. This method does not exploit counter-propagating waves approach and gives insight of nonlinear optical wave behavior within the multilayer amplifying structure. The electromagnetic modelling allows observing the influence of gain saturation on the properties of the RSOA. The shape of longitudinal spatial hole burning within the amplifying layer is also obtained.

articleTitle: A Remote Reflecting Fiber Optic Method for Detecting Liquid Occurrences Over a Distance of 3 Kilometres
publicationTitle: 2023 International Workshop on Fiber Optics on Access Networks (FOAN)
abstract: This article introduces a method for detecting liquids over long distances that is based on measuring the difference in the detected reflected power from the end of a conventional single-mode fiber in different mediums. The power of reflected light is affected by the medium outside the fiber, as well as the maximum distance between the sensor end and the detector. The proposed approach was tested on a length of 3.01 km. An investigation of the greatest distance with commercially available laser diodes (MQW - DFB) and a PIN diode is provided; remote measurements at distances more than 34 km are theoretically possible in ideal conditions. We found that the usage of reflecting connectors is the primary constraint in obtaining theoretically calculated distances.

articleTitle: 3D Printing of Fiber and Waveguide Coupling Components in Polymer
publicationTitle: 2023 International Workshop on Fiber Optics on Access Networks (FOAN)
abstract: The growing need for customized components in emerging fiber optic communication networks stems from the increasing demand for high-speed and reliable data transmission by means of standard and specialty optical fibers, as well as their interconnection with photonic integrated circuits. 3D-printing has emerged as a promising enabling technology in this context, offering the ability to fabricate intricate and customized components. Among different 3D-printing technologies 2-photon polymerization-based direct laser writing (2PP-DLW) excels owing to sub-micrometer resolutions for fast additive manufacturing of optical components in polymer. We present an overview of our latest advancements in design and proof-of-concept demonstration of interfacing components tailored for fibers and short-distance optical interconnects. We demonstrated low-loss waveguides, microstructured waveguides, mode conversion tapers, S-bends and couplers with 2PP-DLW technology fabricated on either on a fiber tip or a planar substrate [1]–[3].

articleTitle: Heterogenous Photonic Integration for Quantum Optical Communication
publicationTitle: 2023 International Workshop on Fiber Optics on Access Networks (FOAN)
abstract: Photonic integrated circuits (PICs) play an important role in telecom and datacom applications. While in the past integrated transceivers were the main driver for technological advances in integrated photonics, nowadays PICs are emerging in various other fields, such as sensing, high-performance computing, quantum technologies, and more [1]. Various material platforms for PICs have been developed and successfully utilized, like III-V semiconductors (InP, GaAs), silicon-based materials (Si, Si<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>, SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>), lithium niobate (LiNbO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>), polymers and others.

articleTitle: Hybrid-Mode Distributed Fiber Sensing with Multiple Parameters Monitoring Ability
publicationTitle: 2023 International Workshop on Fiber Optics on Access Networks (FOAN)
abstract: This article discusses the integration of Brillouin optical time-domain analysis (BOTDA) and Phase-sensitive Optical Time Domain Reflectometry (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Phi-\text{OTDR}$</tex>) for distributed optical fiber sensing systems. Combining these two systems and sharing typical instrumentation can reduce the system cost. On the same 18.7 km optical fiber, temperature, strain, and vibration are detected.

articleTitle: Fiber Bragg Grating Based Optical Sensor: from its Sensing Principle Towards Industrial Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 International Workshop on Fiber Optics on Access Networks (FOAN)
abstract: The presence of optical fiber has continuously increased in our daily life. The first impression on optical fiber for public is the application in communication networks, benefiting from its low signal attenuation over long distance and light weight as a comparison to coaxial cable. On the other hand, other benefits such as resistance against electromagnetic interference and the ability to be multiplexed show a great potential to overcome several limitations what the electric based sensors has encountered now. Therefore, numerous research has carried out on using optical fiber as a sensing element.

articleTitle: Free Space Optical Channel Estimation Based on Deep Learning Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2023 International Workshop on Fiber Optics on Access Networks (FOAN)
abstract: Channel estimation is a key feature for Free Space Optical (FSO) communication systems, necessary to ensure high-quality service and high data rates. Targeting the issue of classical FSO channel estimation, this work introduces a channel estimation scheme based on deep learning algorithms, namely Deep Neural Networks (DNN), Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN), and Recurrent Neural Networks (RNN). To compare with channel estimation techniques using classical algorithms such as Least Squares (LS) and Minimum Mean Square Error (MMSE), we apply these methods. Considering the presence of strong Gamma-Gamma atmospheric turbulence, we study the performance of the proposed structures. The results indicate that the proposed channel estimation schemes based on deep learning algorithms outperform traditional estimation techniques and can approach near-perfect channel estimation. Additionally, they are cost-effective, relatively simple, and offer favorable performance.

articleTitle: Theoretical and Practical Bounds on the Initial Value of Clock Skew Compensation Algorithm Immune to Floating-Point Precision Loss for Resource-Constrained Wireless Sensor Nodes
publicationTitle: 2023 International Workshop on Fiber Optics on Access Networks (FOAN)
abstract: In this paper, we revisit our prior work on clock skew compensation immune to floating-point precision loss and provide practical as well as theoretical bounds on the initial value of the skew-compensated clock based on a systematic analysis of the errors of floating-point operations; by practical bounds, we mean the actual values of the theoretical bounds from the systematic analysis calculated at resource-constrained computing platforms like battery-powered, low-cost wireless sensor nodes equipped with the 32-bit single-precision floating-point format. The numerical examples demonstrate that the proposed practical bounds based on single-precision floating-point format do not violate the theoretical bounds and thereby can guarantee the correctness of the clock skew compensation even on resource-constrained computing platforms.

articleTitle: Access Network Optimization: Impacts of Rising Energy Prices and Volume of Data Traffic
publicationTitle: 2023 International Workshop on Fiber Optics on Access Networks (FOAN)
abstract: T-2 was founded in 2004 as the first alternative operator with the ambition to start the active development of the Slovenian telecommunications market and bring it closer to the developing technologies, which at the time heralded extraordinary changes in the development of the telecommunications market. From 2005 to 2007, we were among the first in Europe to offer services to our clients based on VDSL1, which we later upgraded to VDSL2. At the same time, we started building and offering services based on the Fibre to the Home Point-to-Point technical solution, which in 2018 we replaced with the GPON Point-to-Multipoint solution. We are firmly embedded in the environment in which we operate, we listen to each individual and take the sustainability aspect of business and wider operations into account. Being a company of satisfied employees, we respond to the challenges of profitable growth and are jointly building T-2 into a leading provider on the market. We also focused on other areas such as e-mobility and smart cities. We have more than 450 employees.

articleTitle: Specialty Optical Fibers for Advanced Sensing Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 International Workshop on Fiber Optics on Access Networks (FOAN)
abstract: Optical fiber technology has significantly bolstered the growth of photonic applications in numerous areas such as the telecom infrastructure, a wide range of sensors, vehicle and airplane control, life sciences research, and biomedical diagnosis, therapy, monitoring, and imaging. This tutorial gives an overview of recent developments in diverse configurations of specialty optical fibers and their sensing applications. First the fundamental principles for light guiding in conventional solid-core fibers are presented in order to show how optical fibers function in general. Next, using this background material, various specialty optical fibers with expanded optical, electrical, acoustic, or optoelectronic functionalities are reviewed based on innovations in their unique structures, the use of special combinations of materials, and implementations of light-manipulation technologies. Then an overview of sensing applications in various fields is presented.

articleTitle: NIS2 Impact on Electronic Communications Networks Providers
publicationTitle: 2023 International Workshop on Fiber Optics on Access Networks (FOAN)
abstract: Five years after the deadline for the transposition of the first EU-wide legislation on cybersecurity, known as Directive (EU) 2016/1148 or NIS, ended, the Directive (EU) 2022/2555, otherwise NIS2, entered into force, addressing the limitations and challenges of NIS [1], [2]. NIS2 expands the scope of the previous rules by adding eleven more sectors, introducing new cybersecurity risk and incident management requirements and strengthening the reporting requirements. In terms of categories of operators and providers, NIS2 eliminates this distinction and classifies the entities based on whether they are essential or important, which also determines their supervisory regime. Security and reporting requirements take a risk management approach with a minimum list of basic security elements that need to be applied [3].

articleTitle: Where HFC Stands in Today's Access World: A Comparison with PON, with Systems Engineering Approach
publicationTitle: 2023 International Workshop on Fiber Optics on Access Networks (FOAN)
abstract: The demands for fast and reliable bandwidth has put a lot of pressure on the telecom and cable industry to build a sustainable, flexible, and future-proof network [1]. There are several factors that have had a great impact on increasing of these demands, mainly technological developments. There are also non-technological factors that influence these demands, for example COVID period has shown that working from home office is possible, and at times more productive, which derivatively implies the need of better broadband services for home offices.

articleTitle: Negative Curvature Hollow-Core Photonic Crystal Fibers Sensitivity to Acoustic Vibration in the Audible Spectrum
publicationTitle: 2023 International Workshop on Fiber Optics on Access Networks (FOAN)
abstract: Hollow-Core Photonic Crystal Fibers (HC-PCF) offer a number of advantages over conventional single-mode (SM) optical fibers. In addition to their evaluation of transmission parameters, it is also necessary to deal with their sensitivity to acoustic vibrations, and thus the possibility of use as a sensor. A homodyne Mach-Zehnder interferometer (MZI) was used to assess its sensitivity, while for a reference arm the G.657 fiber was used and HC-PCF for sensing arm. The entire measurement took place in an anechoic chamber with reference measurement of both the acoustic signal source and the use of reference microphones for background noise measurement. The measurement results show a sensitivity to acoustic vibrations up to a frequency of 3 kHz, with a higher sensitivity in the lower frequency band, which could make it possible to significantly increase the sensitivity of today's sensors operating in this frequency range. The results contribute to the understanding and potential application of hollow fibers in distributed optical sensing.

articleTitle: Multiplexing Multi-Gbps Analog Radio-Over-Fiber Links Over a Converged Fiber/FSO Intra-Campus Infrastructure
publicationTitle: 2023 International Workshop on Fiber Optics on Access Networks (FOAN)
abstract: This paper is focused on the experimental demonstration of Analog Over Fiber systems over converged Fiber/Free Space Optical links enabling the X-haul connectivity in beyond 5G and 6G era. More specifically, we present an experimental campaign of Radio over Fiber transmission of diverse waveforms over hybrid Fiber/ Free Space Optical links scenarios. Initially, we present a brief link budget analysis for the Free Space Optical link. The performance of the end-to-end system is assessed in terms of real time error vector magnitude measurements. In parallel, by emulating a wavelength division multiplexing passive optical network topology, the RoF streams are also multiplexed with mobile traffic of an installed X-haul topology, produced by Small Form-factor Pluggable transceivers, and their performance over the converged fiber/FSO architecture is experimentally demonstrated.

articleTitle: Mechanical Reliability and Lifetime of Optical Fibers After 20 Years of Use
publicationTitle: 2023 International Workshop on Fiber Optics on Access Networks (FOAN)
abstract: The Numerous papers have presented models for the mechanical reliability of optical fibres, or the lifetime of optical fibres, has been modelled in many works. Improvement of the mechanical and optical characteristics of standard single-mode fibres requires new tests and analyses. This paper provides an overview of scientific research into the mechanical reliability of optical fibres by some of the largest manufacturers. The investigation of the mechanical reliability and state of optical fibres after 20 years of real usage is the contribution of the paper, which concludes on its own. The contribution of the work is also in the analysis of the conditions under which optical cables - fibers were used. A prediction of the parameters limiting the lifetime of optical fibres was made based on the analyses that were conducted.
